Alexis I. duPont High School
Alexis I. duPont High School
(
A.I.
[
2
]
) is a
public high school
located in
Greenville, Delaware
,
[
3
]
with a
Wilmington
postal address,
[
4
]
is one of the three public high schools offering grades 9–12 in the
Red Clay Consolidated School District
.
[
5
]
During the 2019–2020 school year 807 students were enrolled.
[
6
]
Areas zoned to AI come from portions of
Wilmington
and several suburbs, including
Greenville
, most of
Hockessin
, a portion of
North Star
,
[
7
]
[
8
]
and
Centreville
, as well as nearby
Breck's Mill
.
[
9
]
In Wilmington, it serves the historic districts of
Cool Spring Park
,
[
10
]
Delaware Avenue
,
[
11
]
[
12
]
and
Wawaset Park
.
[
13
]
In 2020, the high school was the site of the first
campaign
event featuring Democratic presidential nominee
Joe Biden
and his running mate
Kamala Harris
.
[
14
]
History
Its namesake was
Alexis I. duPont
.
[
15
]
The same man was the namesake of Alexis I. duPont Middle School, which evolved from the high school.
[
16
]
It originated from the "yellow school house" first established in 1832 and expanded in 1857, the latter assisted by the namesake.
[
15
]
Founded in 1893 under Principal A.R. Spade, Alexis I. duPont High School (AI) was originally a part of the Alexis I. duPont School District.
[
17
]
[
18
]
[
19
]
AI moved to its current location in 1966 from where Alexis I. duPont Middle School stands today.
[
17
]
Both schools left the AI School District in 1978 and were moved into the short-lived
New Castle County School District
, which split into the
Red Clay Consolidated
,
Brandywine
,
Christiana
, and
Colonial
school districts in August 1981.
[
20
]
[
21
]
There were 1,480 students in the 2009-2010 school year. Enrollment was over 1,000 in the 2016-2016 school year. On September 30, 2023, it had 605 students, resulting in it having the smallest enrollment of a public high school in Delaware. It had a significant enrollment decline while the other two traditional public high schools in the district did not experience this.
[
22
]
Academics
In 2021,
U.S. News & World Report
ranked AI #9,632 of more than 18,000 high schools nationally
[
23
]
and
Niche
ranked it #1 of 56 schools in the state of Delaware.
[
24
]
AI's graduation rate for the 2018–2019 academic year was 88%.
[
23
]
Athletics
AI is a member of the
Delaware Interscholastic Athletic Association
(DIAA) and as of 2017 participates in Flight B of the
Blue Hen Conference
.
[
25
]
[
26
]
[
27
]
Sports played within the DIAA league are: football, cross country, field hockey, soccer, volleyball, basketball, swimming, wrestling, baseball, golf, lacrosse, softball, tennis, and track & field.
[
28
]
The ice hockey team is a Division I school within the Delaware Scholastic Hockey Association, which is hosted at the Patriot Ice Center in
Newark
.
[
29
]
[
30
]
Student activities
They have marched in the inaugural parades for
Jimmy Carter
,
[
31
]
George H. W. Bush
,
[
32
]
and
Barack Obama
.
[
33
]
They appeared in
Pasadena's
Tournament of Roses Parade
in 1990, 1995, 1999, 2004, and 2008 and are one of three bands outside of
California
to take part five times.
[
34
]
[
35
]
Other notable appearances include: the
Orange Bowl
(1997, 2000) and
Fiesta Bowl
(2006, 2010); the
St. Patrick's Day Parade
in
Dublin, Ireland
(1993, 1997, 2000, and 2003); the 2002
Queen's Golden Jubilee
;
New Year's Day parades
in
London
(1989, 1992, 1996, 2005, 2009, 2012, and 2017) and the New Year's Parade at
St. Peter's Square
in the
Vatican City
(2007, 2012, and 2015).
[
34
]
[
35
]
[
36
]
The Tiger Marching Band has attended the
6abc Dunkin' Donuts Thanksgiving Day Parade
in
Philadelphia
since at least 1979, the Macy's Thanksgiving parade in New York City and the Latin American and Christmas Parades in Wilmington for many years.
[
37
]
[
38
]
[
39
]
Vocal music at A.I. consists of several different ensembles, including a concert and a chamber choir, designed to meet the variety of needs, talents, and interests of high school vocalists.
[
40
]
The band is a student-run organization in which students, specifically an executive board of seniors, make nearly all of the governing decisions.
[
41
]
Paul L. Parets, who had been the high school's band director since 1976, retired in the spring of 2012.
[
34
]
The band has since been directed by Richard F. Weaver III, who is a 1998 AI alumnus and joined the faculty in 2003.
